title: Artificial intelligence (AI) for breast cancer screening: BreastScreen population-based cohort study of cancer detection.
summary: A commercially available mammography AI algorithm scored cancer likelihood and was compared with practicing radiologists; simulated AI-radiologist arbitration estimated workload and screening outcomes. External evaluation of 108,970 consecutive screens with registry-ascertained interval cancers: AI AUC .83 vs radiologists .93; at prospective threshold sensitivity .67 vs .68 but specificity .81 vs .97. AI-plus-reader simulation reduced reading volume 41.4%, with slightly lower cancer detection rate but detected interval cancers missed at original reading. Real-world retrospective population screening cohort external validation, outcomes linked to registry; simulations are not prospective deployment.
